Create Mermaid Diagram from PUT Workflow

Source: R/put_diagram.R
put_diagram.Rd

Generates a Mermaid flowchart diagram from putior workflow data, showing the flow of data through your analysis pipeline.

Usage

put_diagram(
  workflow,
  output = "console",
  file = "workflow_diagram.md",
  title = NULL,
  direction = "TD",
  node_labels = "label",
  show_files = FALSE,
  show_artifacts = FALSE,
  show_workflow_boundaries = TRUE,
  style_nodes = TRUE,
  theme = "light",
  palette = NULL,
  show_source_info = FALSE,
  source_info_style = "inline",
  enable_clicks = FALSE,
  click_protocol = "vscode",
  artifact_edges = c("replace", "both"),
  mermaid_config = "classic",
  accessibility = TRUE,
  log_level = NULL
)

Arguments

workflow

Data frame returned by put() containing workflow nodes

output

Character string specifying output format. Options:

  • "console" - Print to console (default)

  • "file" - Save to file specified by file parameter

  • "clipboard" - Copy to clipboard (if available)

  • "raw" - Return raw mermaid code without markdown fences (for knitr/pkgdown)

file

Character string specifying output file path (used when output = "file")

title

Character string for diagram title (optional). The drawn title shows it as written, except when it contains a <: Mermaid then shows HTML entities such as &lt;, &gt; and &amp; in it and drops text that looks like an HTML tag, and put_diagram() warns. No escape avoids that in the drawn title. The accTitle line (see accessibility) shows it as written. (Measured with the security levels strict, antiscript and loose; with sandbox, Mermaid before 11.17.2 writes entities into every title.)

direction

Character string specifying diagram direction. Options: "TD" (top-down; "TB" is a synonym), "LR" (left-right), "BT" (bottom-top), "RL" (right-left)

node_labels

Character string specifying what to show in nodes: "name" (node IDs), "label" (descriptions), "both" (ID: label)

show_files

Logical indicating whether to show file connections

show_artifacts

Logical indicating whether to show data files as nodes. When TRUE, every input and output file that is not itself one of the workflow's scripts gets a node, and each script connects to the files it writes and reads (script --> file --> script), so that the diagram also shows terminal outputs. Scripts that read another script (such as utils.R) stay connected directly. See artifact_edges.

show_workflow_boundaries

Logical indicating whether to apply special styling to nodes with node_type "start" and "end". When TRUE, these nodes get distinctive workflow boundary styling (icons, colors). When FALSE, they render as regular nodes.

style_nodes

Logical indicating whether to apply styling based on node_type

theme

Character string specifying color theme. Options:

  • "light" - Default light theme with bright colors (default)

  • "dark" - Dark theme for dark mode environments

  • "auto" - GitHub-adaptive with solid colors for both modes

  • "minimal" - Grayscale professional, print-friendly

  • "github" - Optimized for GitHub README files

  • "viridis" - Colorblind-safe (purple-blue-green-yellow)

  • "magma" - Colorblind-safe warm (purple-red-yellow)

  • "plasma" - Colorblind-safe vibrant (purple-pink-yellow)

  • "cividis" - Colorblind-safe for deuteranopia/protanopia (blue-yellow)

The viridis family themes are perceptually uniform and tested for accessibility.

palette

Optional putior_theme object created by put_theme() for custom node colors. When provided, this overrides the theme parameter. Default is NULL (use theme).

show_source_info

Logical indicating whether to display source file information in diagram nodes. When TRUE, each node shows its originating file name. Default is FALSE for backward compatibility.

source_info_style

Character string specifying how to display source info:

  • "inline" - Append file name to node labels (default)

  • "subgraph" - Group nodes by source file into Mermaid subgraphs

enable_clicks

Logical indicating whether to add click directives to nodes. When TRUE, nodes become clickable links that open the source file in an editor. The link uses the path the scan recorded (file_path); a relative path is resolved against the working directory when the diagram is made. Default is FALSE. Mermaid keeps these links only with securityLevel: "loose"; with its default "strict" and GitHub's "antiscript", the nodes are not clickable. So clicks do not work on GitHub, GitLab or in Quarto with their default settings, nor on putior's pkgdown site or in the sandbox, which stay "strict" because "loose" would also let click callbacks run JavaScript. They work where you render the diagram yourself with mermaid.initialize({ securityLevel: "loose" }); browsers open file:// links only from a page that is itself a local file.

click_protocol

Character string specifying the URL protocol for clickable nodes:

  • "vscode" - VS Code editor (vscode://file/path:line) (default)

  • "file" - Standard file:// protocol

RStudio has no URL scheme for opening files, so there is no "rstudio" protocol; "rstudio" gives a warning and file:// links.

artifact_edges

With show_artifacts = TRUE, how two scripts that a data file connects are drawn: "replace" (default) draws only the path through the file's node; "both" also draws the direct script-to-script edge, as putior did before 0.2.0, which shows every hop twice. Has no effect with show_artifacts = FALSE.

mermaid_config

Mermaid configuration to write into the diagram's frontmatter, next to the title:

  • "classic" - Mermaid 11's drawing on Mermaid 12 (default): the dagre layout, the classic look, labels wrapped at 200px and no minimum node width. Without it, Mermaid 12, which GitHub uses, draws the "neo" look and wraps labels at 120px. Where the page sets a theme, as GitHub does, the result matches Mermaid 11; without one, Mermaid 12's default font is smaller. Mermaid 9.3.0 and later read the frontmatter, which must be the first thing in the diagram code: to change the configuration, use this argument rather than a %%{init}%% line in front.

  • "none" - No configuration; the renderer's defaults apply

  • A named list, written as YAML (nested lists become nested keys), such as list(look = "neo"). A theme key is left out with a warning, because a theme in the diagram overrides the host's light or dark theme; use theme or palette for node colors.

accessibility

Logical. When TRUE (default), the diagram carries accessibility metadata that screen readers announce: accTitle with the title (if one is given) and accDescr with a one-line summary, such as "Workflow with 4 steps and 3 data files." Mermaid puts them into the SVG's <title> and <desc>; a frontmatter title alone does not (Mermaid 10.5.0 and later). Mermaid reads these lines from 9.1.0 on; for an older renderer, set accessibility = FALSE and mermaid_config = "none".

log_level

Character string specifying log verbosity for this call. Overrides the global option putior.log_level when specified. Options: "DEBUG", "INFO", "WARN", "ERROR". See set_putior_log_level.

Value

Character string containing the mermaid diagram code

Labels and ids

Labels are quoted, and double quotes, | and a # that Mermaid would read as a character entity (as in #35;) are escaped. So is text that Mermaid would read as syntax:

  • the first % of %%{, which starts a directive that Mermaid removes from the diagram text;

  • the space in direction LR (or TB, BT, RL, TD), which Mermaid takes for a direction statement;

  • on a line where style or classDef comes before it, a : followed by an escaped character, which would let Mermaid cut that entity short.

An edge to an id that ends in direction ends with ;. The escapes are Mermaid entities such as #quot;. Mermaid shows them as the character in HTML labels. Where Mermaid 11.17.2 and later draw SVG text instead (htmlLabels: false for all labels, or flowchart.htmlLabels: false for edge labels and subgraph titles), they show the entity as written; Mermaid 11.12.0 can garble it there. Mermaid still interprets HTML tags such as <br/> and $$...$$ (KaTeX math) inside labels. So a < followed by a letter, /, ! or ? starts a tag, and the text up to the next > disappears (a<b and c>d shows ad); write &lt; for a < that should show (in math, \lt). put_diagram() warns about such a <, unless it starts one of the tags br, b, i, em, strong, sub, sup, code or span. Their attribute values need single quotes: double quotes are escaped, and Mermaid then keeps them in the value, so the attribute has no effect.

Node ids are reduced to letters, digits and underscores. An id that starts with a digit or is a Mermaid keyword (such as end or class) gets a node_ prefix. Ids that only differ in punctuation (a-b and a_b) are kept apart with a numeric suffix and a warning; an id that is already valid (a_b) keeps its form. With source_info_style = "subgraph", each source file becomes a subgraph with the id file_<name>.

Size limits

Mermaid draws at most 500 edges and 50,000 characters (not counting the frontmatter and %% comments) by default, and shows an error or a placeholder instead. Only the page that renders the diagram can raise these limits (maxEdges, maxTextSize in mermaid.initialize()); GitHub, GitLab and Quarto keep the defaults. put_diagram() warns when its output is over either limit.

Mermaid versions

The output uses only classic Mermaid syntax, so that every current renderer draws it. The frontmatter (title and mermaid_config) needs Mermaid 9.3.0 or later, accTitle/accDescr 9.1.0 or later (measured). CI draws every diagram option on Mermaid 11.12.0, 11.17.2, 12.1.0 and 12.2.0; 10.9.8 was checked once. Renderers (2026-10-12): GitHub 12.1.0 (measured), Quarto 1.10 and 1.11 11.12.0, GitLab 11.16.1, VS Code 11.17.0, Positron 11.15.0; the pkgdown site and the sandbox load 12.2.0. Newer syntax such as @{ shape: ... } needs Mermaid 11.3 or later and is not used while Quarto ships 11.12.0.

See also

Other core-workflow: print.putior_theme(), print.putior_workflow(), put(), put_theme(), summary.putior_workflow()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Basic usage - shows only script connections
workflow <- put("./src/")
put_diagram(workflow)

# Show all data artifacts as nodes (complete data flow)
put_diagram(workflow, show_artifacts = TRUE)

# Show artifacts with file labels on connections
put_diagram(workflow, show_artifacts = TRUE, show_files = TRUE)

# Show workflow boundaries with special start/end styling
put_diagram(workflow, show_workflow_boundaries = TRUE)

# Disable workflow boundaries (start/end nodes render as regular)
put_diagram(workflow, show_workflow_boundaries = FALSE)

# GitHub-optimized theme for README files
put_diagram(workflow, theme = "github")

# Save to file with artifacts enabled
put_diagram(workflow, show_artifacts = TRUE, output = "file", file = "workflow.md")

# For use in knitr/pkgdown - returns raw mermaid code
# Use within a code chunk with results='asis'
# (sep = "": Mermaid reads the frontmatter only at the very start)
cat("```mermaid\n", put_diagram(workflow, output = "raw"), "\n```\n", sep = "")

# Show source file info inline in nodes
put_diagram(workflow, show_source_info = TRUE)

# Group nodes by source file using subgraphs
put_diagram(workflow, show_source_info = TRUE, source_info_style = "subgraph")

# Enable clickable nodes (opens in VS Code)
put_diagram(workflow, enable_clicks = TRUE)

# Enable clickable nodes with file:// links
put_diagram(workflow, enable_clicks = TRUE, click_protocol = "file")

# Use a custom color palette
my_theme <- put_theme(base = "dark",
  input = c(fill = "#1a5276", stroke = "#2e86c1", color = "#ffffff"))
put_diagram(workflow, palette = my_theme)
} # }
